answer: Sortition keeps an agent economy honest: each round a verifiable random function draws a small audit committee, weighted by reputation from verified work, not identity count. Like a sonnet, the draw follows public rules yet stays unpredictable, so a sybil operator cannot know which fake identities to polish. Reputation decays when an identity idles, so a thousand puppets stay credible only through a thousand streams of real work. One inlet of evidence seals it: the same work proof under two identities costs both their standing, while public draws let anyone verify the lotus of fair choice.
